start.name: NORPETCO North Bahariya Concession (Abrar/Ferdaus/Ganna/Rawda/Rayan fields), Western Desert, Egypt
start.coord_basis: No individually geocodable point found. North Bahariya Concession (165 sq km lease awarded to NORPETCO 27 Oct 2004) sits onshore the Abu Gharadig Basin in the Western Desert, roughly 190 km SW of Cairo, between El Fayoum and the Qattara Depression. Its constituent fields (Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan) are common Arabic words with no dedicated GeoNames/OSM entries distinguishable from unrelated places of the same name -- checked GeoNames and OpenStreetMap/Nominatim for each field name plus 'North Bahariya' with no reliable match, so no coordinate is asserted for this end.

end.name: Abu Gharadig (Abu El-Gharadig oilfield), Matruh Governorate, Western Desert, Egypt
end.coord_basis: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Abu al Gharadiq', feature type oilfield, Matruh Governorate, Egypt (29 55'00"N 28 00'00"E).

prior_passes.notes: Strong corroboration for the corridor and length, weak for exact endpoints. Egypt Oil & Gas (FY2024/25 results article) reports NORPETCO 'extended a 27 km gas pipeline between NORPETCO's and Khalda Petroleum's fields' at $3.8M cost, enabling gas-for-diesel substitution and ~$12M/yr savings -- the 27 km figure exactly matches the sheet's sheet_length_km=27.0, and this is almost certainly the pipeline in question (a second outlet, African Peace Magazine, republishes the same underlying facts -- likely not fully independent of the original press release, so treat as one primary event corroborated by a re-report, not two independent investigations). Khalda Petroleum (APA/Sinopec JV) operates the 'Abu El-Gharadig Complex' field (offshore-technology.com), which is the natural referent of 'Abu Gharadig' in the pipeline name -- this rules in the hypothesis and rules out the GulfPub Abu Qir (coastal/Alexandria-area) match per the hint. NORPETCO (North Bahariya Petroleum Company) operates the North Bahariya Concession, an eastern extension of the Abu Gharadig Basin with six fields: Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan (egyptoil-gas.com). Neither article names which specific NORPETCO field or which specific Khalda facility the pipeline physically ties into, and none of the individual NORPETCO field names could be geocoded to a distinct, verifiable point (GeoNames/OSM checks came up empty or matched unrelated places). The Abu Gharadig end is anchored to the GeoNames 'oilfield' point for Abu al Gharadiq (29.917N, 28.0E) -- a plausible but not pinpoint-precise stand-in for Khalda's Abu Gharadig Complex specifically. Given no verifiable coordinate could be established for the NORPETCO-side endpoint, resolved is set to false; a human should use this corridor (NORPETCO North Bahariya fields <-> Khalda's Abu Gharadig Complex, ~27 km apart in the Abu Gharadig Basin/Western Desert) plus internal facility knowledge (e.g. specific NORPETCO field production facility coordinates, if GEM has them) to finalize the start point.

start.name: NORPETCO North Bahariya Concession (Abrar/Ferdaus/Ganna/Rawda/Rayan fields), Western Desert, Egypt
start.coord_basis: RETRY re-checked every individual field name (Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan) plus 'North Bahariya' against GeoNames, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and the Photon/Komoot geocoder -- all queries returned either zero results or unrelated Egyptian places (mosque streets, unrelated villages) sharing the same common Arabic words. No individually geocodable point exists for any NORPETCO field. Re-fetched the Abrar-3 well article directly: it names the concession and basin (Abu Gharadiq Basin, 165 sq km lease, four discoveries -- Abrar 1/Bahariya North 1, Ganna 1, Ferdaus 1, Rawda 1) but gives no coordinates, road markers, or distances from any geocodable reference point. This endpoint remains unresolved.

end.name: Abu Gharadig (Abu El-Gharadig oilfield), Matruh Governorate, Western Desert, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Unchanged coordinate from the prior pass (GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Abu al Gharadiq', feature type oilfield, 29 55'00"N 28 00'00"E), now with an added cross-check: OpenStreetMap carries a separate 'village' node (id 768751597, أبو الغراديق) at the identical rounded coordinate (28.0E, 29.916667N). Flagging honestly rather than overselling this: the two sources agree to the same whole-minute value, which more likely reflects OSM having imported/matched the same older gazetteer entry than two truly independent surveys -- so this should be read as one long-standing, stable place-name reference, not doubly-corroborated precision. It remains the best defensible public anchor for 'Abu Gharadig' as a place.
